title: Romulus and Remus
objective: After this level you can retell Rome’s founding legend and explain why Romans valued it.
summary: Legend says twin sons of Mars, nursed by a she-wolf, founded Rome, and Romulus killed Remus. Historians treat it as legend, not history.

cards.headline: Every Roman knew how their city began: with twins, a wolf and a killing.
Raised by a wolf
cards.body: In the legend, the twins Romulus and Remus were sons of the war god Mars. Abandoned as babies beside the river Tiber, they were found and nursed by a she-wolf. The image of the wolf and the twins became one of Rome’s best-known symbols.

cards.headline: A city named in blood
cards.body: When the grown twins founded their city, they quarreled over it, and Romulus killed Remus. The new city took Romulus’s name. Roman writers retold the story for centuries, uncomfortable parts included.

cards.headline: Legend, not history
cards.body: Romans also claimed descent from Aeneas, a Trojan prince who fled the fall of Troy to Italy. Historians treat both stories as legend, written down centuries after the events they describe. They still matter, because they show how Romans saw themselves.

cards.headline: Founding legend: known
learned: Legend: twin sons of Mars founded Rome
Romulus killed Remus; the city took his name

questions.prompt: In the legend, what nursed the abandoned Romulus and Remus?
questions.explanation: A she-wolf found and nursed the twins, an image that became a symbol of Rome.

questions.prompt: Why do historians treat the Romulus and Remus story as legend?

options.label: It was written down centuries after the events
Archaeology shows Rome was never founded
options.rationale: Rome was founded; the story is the question.

questions.explanation: The founding stories were recorded long after the events, so they tell us more about how Romans saw themselves.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: Romans dated the founding to 753 BCE. How did the legend explain the city’s name?

options.label: It was named after the Tiber
It was named after the she-wolf

questions.explanation: After Romulus killed Remus, the new city took Romulus’s name.
